about.en:
ActionxPeace is UWC Spain's experiential peace-education programme. Sixty teenagers from different countries and backgrounds live together for five days and work on identity, empathy, coexistence, conflict transformation and peacebuilding through workshops, dialogue, outdoor activities and community life. Participants leave with practical conflict-transformation tools and a sense of their own role as changemakers.

It is one of the few international residential programmes aimed at secondary-school students rather than adults, and a good taste of the United World Colleges approach to education for peace.

The seminar is organised by UWC Spain and published on the SALTO-YOUTH European Training Calendar. It runs in Nambroca (Toledo), Spain on 4 December 2026 – 8 December 2026. It is for 60 participants. Who it is for: young people born between 2009 and 2011 (aged about 15–17) from diverse backgrounds, plus youth leaders. Participants must be residents of: all countries: Erasmus+ Programme countries, Partner Countries neighbouring the EU and other countries in the world. Working language: English and Spanish (bilingual programme).

Costs: Course fee €470, covering full-board shared accommodation at El Casar de la Inesa (Nambroca, Toledo), meals, materials and all activities. Ten need-based scholarships are available for Spanish and international participants. Travel is not reimbursed. Applications close on 31 October 2026 (24:00 UTC); selection results are expected by 23 November 2026.

about.en:
Resilient Roots trains youth workers to facilitate inclusive, trauma-informed group processes through embodiment, dialogue, nature connection and practical facilitation tools. Module I (8–15 November 2026, Facilitating Climate Dialogue Foundations) is listed here; Module II (Hosting Emergence, 13–20 December 2026) can be booked separately and requires Module I or a previous Pathways course.

The organiser asks applicants to write in their own words: applications written with AI are not considered.

The training course is organised by Pathways Courses and published on the SALTO-YOUTH European Training Calendar. It runs in Steckborn (Schloss Glarisegg), Switzerland on 8 November 2026 – 15 November 2026 (Module II on 13–20 December 2026 is optional). It is for 25–30 participants. Who it is for: youth workers, educators, activists and facilitators working with climate anxiety, uncertainty and group processes. Participants must be residents of: Romania, France, Italy, Denmark and Switzerland (the organiser accepts only these countries). Working language: English.

Costs: Sliding-scale participation contribution. Limited places funded by Movetia (the Swiss national agency) are available for eligible youth workers; self-funded participation is also possible. Accommodation, food and travel details are on the organiser's website (pathways-courses.org/resilient-roots). Applications close on 1 November 2026 (24:00 UTC); selection results are expected by 7 November 2026.

Sessions cover audience engagement, photography, visual storytelling, graphic content and social-media strategy, with the city of Cairo as the creative backdrop. By the end, each participant presents an audience-focused campaign.

With only 12 places it is an intimate workshop, and one of the few activities on the European Training Calendar hosted in the Arab world and open to participants from any country.

Costs: No participation fee, but this is a self-funded activity: participants pay their own travel, accommodation and food. On request the organisers can arrange stay, meals, local transport and visits. No travel reimbursement. about.en:
LIMITLESS is built for people who wear too many hats: project coordinators, grant writers and founders stuck in reactive mode as funding and rules change. Over seven days, Synergy Bulgaria uses its coaching-based Synergy Method to help participants step out of firefighting, prevent burnout and redefine how they lead and create impact.

Synergy has run non-formal education and ESC volunteering programmes since 2013, and the course is aimed at people bringing real challenges from their organisations rather than general curiosity.

The training course is organised by Synergy Bulgaria and published on the SALTO-YOUTH European Training Calendar. It runs in Stara Zagora, Bulgaria on 11 November 2026 – 17 November 2026. It is for 24 participants. Who it is for: people aged 18+ who run or are in the core team of an NGO, or social entrepreneurs working on impact-driven projects; comfortable in English and able to attend all seven days. Participants must be residents of: Erasmus+ Programme countries. Working language: English.

Costs: Participation fee €75. Accommodation (shared rooms at the Youthopia Center, Stara Zagora), three meals a day and materials are covered by Synergy Bulgaria. Travel is reimbursed up to the Erasmus+ distance-band limit. Applications close on 8 November 2026 (24:00 UTC); selection results are expected by 9 November 2026.

about.en:
Equal Ground is ENRMSC's quarterly dialogue series. The first session asks what meaningful participation looks like when communities are not just invited to the table but can shape decisions, policies and action. Through contributions from people with lived experience and participatory exchange, participants look at barriers to participation, the role of youth workers and how organisations can turn community perspectives into action.

It is a short, practical entry point for anyone working on inclusion, migration or youth participation, and a way to meet the network behind the larger ENRMSC Forum in Warsaw in April 2027.

The online forum is organised by European Network of Refugee, Migrant and Stateless Changemakers (ENRMSC) and published on the SALTO-YOUTH European Training Calendar. It runs online on 10 November 2026. It is for 50 participants. Who it is for: youth workers, youth leaders, trainers, community practitioners and people with lived experience of migration or statelessness. Participants must be residents of: all countries: Erasmus+ Programme countries, Partner Countries neighbouring the EU and other countries in the world. Working language: English.

Costs: Free of charge. Online, so no accommodation or travel is involved. Applications close on 9 November 2026 (24:00 UTC); selection results are expected by 10 November 2026.

It shows how arts and creativity can help communication and engagement, especially with young people who take part in different ways, and gives practical ideas for adapting activities and methods.

about.en:
Each day of Art for Inclusion focuses on a different artistic approach: music, movement and dance, visual arts, theatre and art therapy, plus mindfulness for wellbeing and self-awareness. Participants also visit local organisations working on inclusion and diversity in Gdańsk. The aim is to give educators concrete arts-based methods to overcome communication barriers, encourage self-expression and adapt activities to people with different abilities, backgrounds and needs.

From 1 April to 30 November 2027 participants work online in peer groups on the real tensions in their projects, then meet for an in-person Co-Lab in Germany on 3–10 July 2027. The focus is less on showcasing a project and more on letting the process challenge and develop both the work and the person.

The accelerator programme is organised by Melton Foundation and published on the SALTO-YOUTH European Training Calendar. It runs in Online + Co-Lab in Germany, Germany on 1 April 2027 – 30 November 2027 (online April–November 2027; in-person Co-Lab in Germany, 3–10 July 2027). It is for a cohort of participants. Applications close on 15 November 2026 (24:00 UTC); selection results are expected by 16 December 2026.

about.en:
Baltic Regional Fund (BRF) is an NGO in Riga dedicated to fostering civil society development, social inclusion, and intercultural dialogue through non-formal education. As a central component of its youth work, the foundation has a Youth Studio BaMbuss, which is a multifunctional and progressive space in Riga providing a safe environment for young people to learn and grow. As a volunteer, you will be actively involved in the daily life of BRF and #jsBaMbuss, supporting ongoing activities and helping to organise events, community activities, workshops and information campaigns on topics relevant to young people and to you, like art, book, language or sports clubs, as well as activities on EU values and youth opportunities. You will have the chance to develop your own initiatives and explore different cultures.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by BALTIJAS REGIONALAIS FONDS in Riga, Latvia; activity period 32 weeks within 1 December 2026 – 31 July 2027. Topics: Social challenges Education and training Creativity and culture. The placement is open to young people (18–30) resident in: Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Georgia, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Moldova, Montenegro, Netherlands, North Macedonia, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Ukraine. Project code: 2026-1-LV02-ESC51-VTJ-000401987.

Living and learning: Volunteers will be accommodated in an apartment with two floors together with other 6 volunteers from the project and will have a separate room. The rooms have furniture, pillows and blankets, linen. The house has a common area, kitchen fully equipped with necessary things, WiFi, washing machine, a toilet and shower in each floor. If you are interested to take part, fill the online application form: https://forms.gle/nyeFmmBrRsnVwpTM6 As in every ESC project, volunteers get pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

Host's profile: We would be especially glad if you enjoy working in a team, communicating with young people and contributing to a creative environment. Interest in photography, video filming or editing, social media communication, and organising events would be a great advantage. If you feel confident leading workshops or trying out new ideas with youngsters in our youth studio, you will have plenty of opportunities to do so and to grow your abilities along the way.

about.en:
Please apply through the application system on this website: www.logo.at/esc InterAktion is a non-profit organisation in Austria working with young people and communities in the fields of youth work, inclusion, intercultural learning and European cooperation. Our activities take place mainly in Graz and Trofaiach and include workshops, youth exchanges and training courses. Human rights, sustainability and active participation are at the heart of our work. We aim to create welcoming and accessible spaces where young people can learn from each other, develop new skills, share experiences and become involved in their communities. As a volunteer, you will become part of our small team and create activities for young people, especially those with fewer opportunities.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by InterAktion - Verein für ein interkulturelles Zusammenleben in Graz, Austria; activity period 44 weeks within 4 January 2027 – 31 December 2027. Topics: Social challenges Citizenship and democratic participation Education and training. The placement is open to young people (18–30) resident in: Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Georgia, Germany, Greece, Greenland, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Kosovo, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Moldova, Montenegro, Netherlands, North Macedonia, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Türkiye, Ukraine. Project code: 2026-1-AT01-ESC51-VTJ-000400771.

Living and learning: The project provides the standard ESC monthly rates for Austria: €330 for food and €210 pocket money (according to the program guide). Accommodation will be provided in a student residence , where you will have your own room and share a kitchen/ bathroom with other students or volunteers in Graz. The Klimaticket for Styria is possible as well. We will have a bike for you. Volunteers take part in On-Arrival Training and Mid-Term Training provided by the Austrian National Agency. Volunteers receive continuous support from experienced youth workers and trainers. We want volunteering experience to be a learning opportunity for both the volunteer and the organization. As in every ESC project, volunteers get pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Arts and culture inspire, transform, and unite. At EERco, through the European Solidarity Corps, we harness this power to build a greener, more inclusive future. We open doors for young people with fewer opportunities to launch projects with strong social impact. In parks and public spaces, we merge creativity with sustainability—using recycled and reclaimed materials to upgrade outdoor areas and honor their history. Digital tools amplify our mission, tracking energy use, cutting waste, and sharing eco-friendly practices across communities. We nurture talented young artists who may lack resources and host lively events that spark dialogue on green living and social solidarity. Our actions uplift local neighborhoods, turning shared spaces into vibrant hubs of creativity and care.

about.en:
A forest is a living system made of relationships. Starting from this idea, a team of young international volunteers will spend Christmas in Buccino, a small village in inland Southern Italy, as a temporary transformative community. A different Christmas: not about shopping, but about people, nature and traditions, shared with a welcoming local community. Volunteers will plant agroforestry lines at the “Mimì & Peppino” Pedagogical Garden in Buccino, at the Cantiere Educativo in Postiglione and, with Hariba, within the Habitat Lab project in Oliveto Citra, preparing planting areas, mulching, composting, protecting young trees and creating habitats for biodiversity. about.en:
Join a team of 7 international volunteers in Sofia, Bulgaria, for a 59-day European Solidarity Corps experience starting on 15 January! Together with Infinite Opportunities Association (IOA), you will promote human rights, diversity, inclusion, equality, and active citizenship. You will prepare and deliver interactive workshops in schools, develop new non-formal education activities and materials for teachers and youth workers, and explore topics such as discrimination, stereotypes, and hate speech. You will also create social media posts, photos, and videos to promote IOA's work, participate in public events and campaigns to represent the organisation, and engage with local communities. Additionally, you will contribute ideas to educational initiatives, including our BARABAR human rights board game.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps team volunteering hosted by VAZMOZHNOSTI BEZ GRANITSI in Sofia, Bulgaria; activity period 8 weeks (15 January 2027 – 14 March 2027). Topics: Social challenges Citizenship and democratic participation Education and training. The placement is open to young people (18–30) resident in: Albania, Austria, Belarus, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Georgia, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Moldova, Montenegro, Netherlands, North Macedonia, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Ukraine. Project code: 2026-1-BG01-ESC51-VTJ-000401138.

Living and learning: Accommodation will be provided in shared apartments in Sofia, close to our office, the city centre, and a park. You will live alongside the other team volunteers and two long-term European Solidarity Corps volunteers, giving you the opportunity to exchange cultures and build friendships. Room and apartment arrangements will be confirmed before arrival. You will receive a food allowance, pocket money, and a public transport card. You will receive training from IOA on human rights, diversity, inclusion, and non-formal education. You will learn how to design and facilitate interactive workshops, develop educational activities for schools, and create engaging social media content. You will also gain practical experience in awareness-raising campaigns and public events. As in every ESC project, volunteers get pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
The animal rescue organisation “Lesė” was founded in 2007. In the shelter, we have cats and dogs waiting for their forever homes. Our goals include finding new homes for homeless animals, providing them with temporary shelter and veterinary treatment, carrying out “Catch-Neuter-Release” programs for cats, and much more. Our mission is to provide high-quality supervision for sheltered animals and share information about animal welfare with the public. Our volunteers are caring for cats and dogs in the shelter: feeding, cleaning cages, walking the dogs, cleaning cat rooms, getting them ready for photoshoots and preparing them for the trip to the veterinary office. Besides that, they are taking part in all sorts of events and festivals to spread the word about animal welfare and volunteering. We are looking for a volunteer for a 10-12 month placement (starting in February 2027).

Project code: 2024-2-LT02-ESC51-VTJ-000290214.

Living and learning: Your volunteer experience in Vilnius should be about impact, not stress. That’s why we provide a comfortable living setup in a shared flat where you can connect with other international volunteers while still enjoying the privacy of your own bedroom. We provide a monthly transport pass and a stipend for your living expenses, leaving you free to explore everything Lithuania has to offer. We know that moving to a new country is a big step, which is why we’ve built a comprehensive support network. From the structured National Agency trainings to the regular, friendly check-ins with your coordinating organisation, you’ll always have a roadmap for your progress. This program revolves around soil regeneration via permaculture and syntropic agroforestry techniques. We are reviving 30 hectares of degraded land to serve as a model for eco living and provide ways to ensure food and water security via regenerative practices such as Sytropic agriculture. This agroforestry technique advocates cooperation in nature as opposed to competition and highlights the role of diversity in creating a healthy ecosystem. The site is being transformed into a public park filled with biodiversity and a green playground for hosting our yearly music and art festival. You will be participating in various activities such as creating and maintaining agroforestry systems, organic gardening, developing the compost area and regenerative landscaping.

about.en:
For many people, permaculture mainly means caring about the garden and plants. Permaculture however is a wider concept that includes in addition to earth care, caring about the people and their needs. It is based on relationships that should grow and support each other. Growing inside can be approached either in a philosophical, emotional, or mental way in our vision and understanding of the world. Growing outside can be related to gardening, relationships, nature, or our skills. Perma comes from permanent –something that can be sustainable. Culture is a complex of specific spiritual, material, intellectual and emotional traits of a society or social group, which also includes a common way of life, lifestyle, value system, traditions, and faith. We will explore together “What is perma-Culture?” not only in a material way, but also in philosophical, social, and also personal way.

about.en:
The ESC Project "Change Support Volunteer" offers young European volunteers a meaningful experience of personal growth and social engagement. Volunteers will join the CSV Brescia team and support the promotion of volunteering and European mobility opportunities. Their tasks will include creating social media content, supporting communication activities, helping at info stands and public events, and facilitating workshops in schools. Volunteers will also contribute to the operational management of mobility projects and other initiatives run by the organisation. They will support the Volunteer Orientation Desk and participate in awareness-raising activities on volunteering, Erasmus+, the European Union and the Agenda 2030.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by CENTRO DI SERVIZIO PER IL VOLONTARIATO BRESCIA - ETS in Brescia, Italy; activity period 11 months (15 January 2027 – 21 December 2027). Topics: Citizenship and democratic participation Creativity and culture. The placement is open to young people (18–30) resident in: Albania, Armenia, Austria, Belarus, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Georgia, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Kosovo, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Moldova, Montenegro, Netherlands, North Macedonia, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Ukraine. Project code: 2024-2-IT03-ESC51-VTJ-000266114.

Living and learning: Volunteers will be accommodated in a shared apartment in the city centre of Brescia. The apartment offers comfortable shared rooms, a fully equipped kitchen, Wi-Fi, and common spaces where volunteers can spend time together and enjoy intercultural exchange. Volunteers will receive a monthly food allowance of €200 , a local public transport pass to reach to the Office (15 minutes by bus), and €6 per day as pocket money. Volunteers will follow a structured learning path combining hands-on experience with training opportunities. At the beginning, they will take part in an orientation session covering project activities, cultural integration, and practical aspects of the experience. As in every ESC project, volunteers get pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Fridhem offers a unique long-term volunteer experience in a close-knit ecological community in Sweden. Focused on sustainability, permaculture, shared living, and personal growth, the project gives volunteers the chance to develop practical skills while becoming part of everyday community life. Activities change with the seasons and may include gardening, growing and harvesting food, communal cooking with local and homegrown ingredients, building and restoration projects, maintenance, workshops, and community events. Volunteers are encouraged to contribute their own ideas, interests, and strengths. Life at Fridhem is built around cooperation, cultural exchange, and learning together. Volunteers receive regular support from a dedicated coordinator through meetings and daily check-ins.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Stiftelsen Stjärnsund in Stjärnsund, Sweden; activity period 48 weeks within 1 January 2027 – 30 May 2027. Topics: Environment and natural protection Health and wellbeing Creativity and culture Disaster Preparedness. The placement is open to young people (18–30) resident in: Albania, Armenia, Austria, Belarus, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Georgia, Germany, Greece, Greenland, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Moldova, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Russia, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Ukraine. Project code: 2026-1-SE02-ESC51-VTJ-000469641.

Living and learning: Enjoy a private 1-room cabin or tiny house on wheels. Shared kitchen & bathroom in volunteer house with access to extra facilities in the main center building. Shared kitchen heated by making wood fires in the winter. Vegetarian food, mainly cooked and prepared together by volunteers. Green travel to and from the center. Pickup at the local train station in Hedemora (20 min drive). Volunteers receive hands-on training in sustainability, permaculture, gardening, food growing, communal cooking, fermenting, wild foraging, and ecological living. Participants can also learn practical building and restoration skills, including natural building techniques such as timber-framing and clay construction. As in every ESC project, volunteers get pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

Our organization was founded by youth workers, teachers, volunteers, who share the vision of creating equal opportunities for everyone. As a volunteer, you will support educational and social activities for children in nurseries, kindergartens, and primary schools, while also contributing to activities in high schools and centers for adults with disabilities.

about.en:
As a volunteer at Harmony Home, a residential facility for seniors with complex care needs, you will become part of a team that provides both health and social care, with a strong focus on social activation and meaningful everyday life for older people. Your main role will be to spend time with residents and support leisure and activation activities. This may include playing musical instruments, reading together, talking and reminiscing, browsing books, playing various games, or simply being present and offering companionship. You will also assist with group and outdoor activities, such as walks, excursions, and larger social or cultural events. In cooperation with the staff, you may help with the organisation of major events and support the pleasant atmosphere of the facility by assisting with the maintenance of indoor and outdoor spaces, including gardens and common areas.

Topics: Social challenges Health and wellbeing Creativity and culture. The placement is open to young people (18–30) resident in: Armenia, Austria, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Canary Islands, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, French Guiana, French Polynesia, Georgia, Germany, Greece, Greenland, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Jordan, Kosovo, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Madeira, Malta, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Saint Martin (french part), Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Türkiye, Ukraine. Living and learning: Volunteers receive a daily stipend of 7 EUR. In addition, a 9 EUR per day food allowance is provided. The project also covers the costs of Czech language lessons, local transportation, and all other expenses directly related to the volunteering activity. We provide accommodation in a private apartment located about a 10-minute walk from the city centre. The apartment has a shared living room with a kitchen, a bathroom, and a separate toilet. The main learning process takes place through active participation in daily life at Harmonie Retirement House. Volunteers build meaningful relationships, gain practical experience, and develop communication, social, and teamwork skills in a real-life environment. As in every ESC project, volunteers get pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

Your role will focus mainly on activation and leisure activities, helping children use their time in a positive and constructive way. You will also assist with school preparation, especially in foreign languages (mainly English), and take part in organising and leading club and extracurricular activities based on your interests and skills. This opportunity is ideal for volunteers who enjoy working with young people, are creative and proactive, and want to support children in their personal development, education, and social inclusion.

about.en:
Our project will take place in Palermo, involving 14 young people aged 18-30. The project aims to raise awareness of the value of non-formal education as a tool for active participation and social inclusion, offering opportunities for both personal and professional development. Specific objectives include: Promoting the well-being and educational growth of minors in the Ballarò and Dannisini neighbourhoods, particularly those facing sociocultural and economic difficulties, by engaging with schools, families, the third sector, and local institutions. Empowering young volunteers with knowledge and skills on gender equality, countering violence and stereotypes. Providing opportunities for skill-building in various areas, including office management, European funds administration, and project planning.

about.en:
You help young people build the digital and AI skills that matter today. You support our trainers in workshops on AI tools such as ChatGPT, Midjourney, Perplexity and Copilot, on cybersecurity and on spotting fake news, building on projects like "Szkolna Akademia Cyberbezpieczenstwa 2.0" and "Mlodzi Eksploratorzy AI". Great if you enjoy technology and helping others learn. Support our digital and AI education, including the school programme Szkolna Akademia Cyberbezpieczenstwa 2.0. We teach young people digital skills, AI tools (ChatGPT, Midjourney, Perplexity, Copilot), cybersecurity and how to spot fake news. What you do: help trainers prepare workshops, set up equipment, co-create learning materials, give technical support during sessions and bring an intercultural element by sharing your own experience.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Klaster Innowacji Społecznych in Gliwice, Poland; activity period 26 weeks within 1 September 2026 – 31 May 2027. Topics: Education and training. The placement is open to young people (18–30) resident in: Armenia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, France, Georgia, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, North Macedonia, Norway, Portugal, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden. Project code: 2026-1-PL01-ESC51-VTJ-000402768.

Living and learning: The foundation provides a furnished room in Gliwice, within easy reach of our office. Volunteers receive a monthly food allowance (6 EUR per day) and pocket money (6 EUR per day), about 360 EUR per month in total. Travel costs to and from Poland are reimbursed according to European Solidarity Corps distance bands, and every volunteer is covered by the ESC insurance scheme. The volunteer receives preparatory support before departure, on-arrival training and a mid-term evaluation organised by the Polish National Agency, weekly Polish language support plus access to the Online Language Support (OLS), a personal mentor with regular one-to-one meetings, and ongoing support from the coordinating team. As in every ESC project, volunteers get pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
The organization runs two youth-oriented programs. “Tranzitas” is designed for young people aged 12–14, while “Sofkė” is an open youth space and street-work program for those aged 14–28. Tranzitas is built around several key elements: group activities, hands-on experiential weekends, and after-school sessions. All programs are created for young people who face social or emotional challenges at school, at home, with peers, or while trying to enter the job market. The main goal is to help young people understand themselves better, strengthen important personal skills, and feel more confident navigating everyday life.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by The Blessed J. Matulaitis social center in Vilnius, Lithuania; activity period 12 months (2 August 2027 – 23 July 2028). Topics: Social challenges Environment and natural protection Education and training. The placement is open to young people (18–30) resident in: Austria, Belgium, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Georgia, Germany, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Türkiye, Ukraine. Project code: 2025-1-LT02-ESC51-VTJ-000347236.

Living and learning: Project provides a travel costs reimbursement from volunteer country of residence to Lithuania and back home after the project. The amount of reimbursement depends on the distance between sending and hosting countries. Volunteer will live in a shared apartment together with other volunteers, but in separate rooms. All the utilities are going to be payed by the organization. Volunteers take part in several trainings to support their journey. Before departure, a preparatory session is held by the sending organization. Soon after arrival, the Lithuanian National Youth Agency offers on-arrival training. Midway through the project, a mid-term seminar brings volunteers together to reflect, share experiences, and recharge. As in every ESC project, volunteers get pre-departure and on-arrival training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

The activity will prioritise young people with fewer opportunities, including NEETs, young people from low-income or migrant backgrounds. Through intercultural activities, community events and awareness campaigns, volunteers will promote solidarity, equality, inclusion, tolerance and respect for diversity. The project will empower young people to challenge stereotypes, strengthen their sense of European belonging and become active promoters of EU values within their communities. See our 2026
